Import a file as a new document

Source: R/doc-import.R
grist_doc_import.Rd

grist_doc_import() uploads a file and creates a new document from it in a workspace. It's the quickest way to start from data you already have in a file. To load several related tables with their types and references, see grist_import().

Usage

grist_doc_import(path, workspace, name = NULL, server = NULL, options = NULL)

Arguments

path

Path to the file to upload.

workspace

A workspace ID, as listed by grist_workspaces().

name

Name for the new document. If NULL, Grist names it after the file.

server

URL of the Grist server, such as "https://docs.getgrist.com" or "https://myteam.getgrist.com". For a self-hosted server, include the team path if needed, e.g. "http://localhost:8484/o/docs". Defaults to the server in doc if doc is a URL, then the GRIST_SERVER environment variable, then "https://docs.getgrist.com".

options

A grist_request_options() object. If NULL, the default from getOption("gristmillr.request_options") or grist_request_options() is used.

Value

A grist_doc() for the new document.

File formats

Grist reads .grist, .csv, .xlsx and .json files. A .grist file becomes a copy of that document. A CSV or JSON file becomes one table named after the file, and an Excel workbook one table per sheet. Column types are guessed from the values, so whole numbers arrive as Numeric and not Int, and nothing links the tables. Use grist_columns_modify() to change types afterwards. A JSON file must hold an array of objects.

See also

Other docs: grist_doc(), grist_doc_create(), grist_doc_download(), grist_request()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc_import("pets.csv", workspace = 1234, name = "Pets")
grist_tables(doc)
grist_records(doc, "Pets")
}
